name: data-viz
summary: The product's charts, stat tiles, topology graph and dashboard grid — a decision GUIDE, not a web component. Charts are Highcharts v10, topology is Cytoscape, the dashboard grid is vue-grid-layout: all app-rendered and licensed/heavy, so the DS does not ship an obs-* for them. The DS now ALSO ships 32 CAPTURED chart configs (9 categories) you can copy — see `chartLibrary` / `charts/` in this package / the showcase charts pages. Use this to pick the RIGHT visualisation type and colour/token it on-brand, then render it with the product's Chart/Graph/Widgets component (in-repo) or STOP-and-ASK (standalone). The one SHIPPABLE element in this family is obs-metric-picker — the metric SELECTOR that AUTHORS a visualization (pick/drag an entity’s counters onto a chart/widget); the charts it feeds stay app-rendered guides.
selectHint: Any CHART / graph / gauge / KPI tile / heatmap / topology map / dashboard grid: pick the type via decisionFlow, colour from chart-palette, then render with the product's Chart/Graph/Widgets component. No obs-* — standalone => STOP and ASK.
decisionFlow: Rendering DATA as a visual? First pick the TYPE by the question you're answering, THEN render it (see the 'how' note below).
A single NUMBER? -> kpi-tile / metro tile. The number only means something vs a threshold/range? -> gauge.
Change over TIME? -> trend-line (default), area (volume / stacked-over-time), or sparkline (inline in a table cell/tile).
COMPARE discrete categories? -> bar-column (long/many labels -> horizontal bar; few -> column; stack for sub-parts). Just the leaders? -> topn.
Part-to-WHOLE? -> pie-donut (<=5 slices) or treemap (hierarchy / many parts).
DENSITY across two dimensions (host x time)? -> heatmap. CORRELATION between two metrics? -> scatter-bubble.
FLOW between nodes? -> sankey-flow (volume) or topology-graph (a pan/zoom network/dependency map).
STATUS / duration over time (SLO, availability)? -> timeline-xrange. By GEOGRAPHY? -> geo-map. A trace/call-stack? -> flame-graph.
A whole DASHBOARD of these? -> widget-grid (resizable tiles).

HOW to render (important): these are drawn by the PRODUCT'S engines (Highcharts v10 for charts, Cytoscape for topology-graph, vue-grid-layout for widget-grid) — NOT framework-agnostic obs-* components. In the product repo -> use the product's Chart / Graph / Widgets components with the type above; colour series from tokens/chart-palette.json (categorical, NOT --primary navy); use severity tokens for status/threshold colours; theme with DS tokens; use data-viz-tooltips for hover. STANDALONE (outside the repo) -> there is still NO obs-chart web component, BUT the DS now ships 32 CAPTURED configs (see `chartLibrary` / `charts/manifest.json`): copy the matching fixture's `config` and render with Highcharts v10 (`Highcharts.chart(el, config)`); the custom-engine types carry a `result` payload instead. Mind the known gaps (unserialised formatter fns; dark-theme capture).

states.name: loading
states.what: data pending — show the widget/chart skeleton or spinner, keep the tile chrome

states.name: empty
states.what: no data for the range — the Highcharts no-data-to-display message / an empty-state, not a blank box

states.name: error
states.what: query failed — an inline error in the tile, not a broken chart

trend-line.useWhen: a metric changing over time (one or a few series) — the default trend
trend-line.dontUse: comparing unrelated discrete categories (-> bar-column); a single headline number (-> kpi-tile)

area.useWhen: a trend where magnitude/volume matters, or stacked composition over time
area.dontUse: many overlapping series (fills occlude — use line)

bar-column.useWhen: compare a value across discrete categories; many/long labels -> horizontal bar, few -> vertical column; stack for sub-parts

pie-donut.useWhen: part-to-whole with a SMALL number of slices (<=5)
pie-donut.dontUse: >5 slices or comparing precise values (-> bar); a hierarchy (-> treemap)

gauge.useWhen: a single value read against a threshold/range (solid gauge / radial)
gauge.dontUse: a trend over time (-> line); a plain number with no threshold (-> kpi-tile)

kpi-tile.useWhen: a single headline number (optionally with a trend arrow / sparkline) — metro tile / KPI card
kpi-tile.dontUse: a value that only makes sense against a range (-> gauge)

sparkline.useWhen: an inline micro-trend inside a table cell or a tile (no axes)
sparkline.dontUse: a standalone chart needing axes/legend (-> line)
sparkline.example: a 7-day trend in each row of a monitors table

heatmap.useWhen: density/intensity across TWO dimensions (e.g. host x time)
heatmap.dontUse: a single series over time (-> line)
heatmap.example: response-time intensity per host across the day

topn.useWhen: a ranked list of the top N items by a value (with inline bars)

scatter-bubble.useWhen: correlation / distribution between two metrics; bubble adds a third (size)

sankey-flow.dontUse: a network topology you can pan/zoom (-> topology-graph)

treemap.useWhen: hierarchical part-to-whole sized by area; many parts

timeline-xrange.useWhen: status/duration bars over time (SLO windows, gantt, availability segments)
timeline-xrange.example: SLO up/down segments across a month

geo-map.useWhen: a value by geography (choropleth via Highmaps, or markers via Leaflet tiles)

flame-graph.useWhen: trace / call-stack profiling (APM/RUM) — rendered with d3-flame-graph, not Highcharts
flame-graph.dontUse: anything that isn't a call/span hierarchy

anomaly-forecast.useWhen: a trend line overlaid with anomaly and/or forecast bands (licensed AI/ML)
anomaly-forecast.dontUse: a plain trend with no ML overlay (-> line)
anomaly-forecast.example: predicted CPU with a forecast band

topology-graph.useWhen: a pan/zoom node-edge NETWORK or dependency map (Cytoscape) — topology, APM service map, NetRoute path
topology-graph.dontUse: a flow volume diagram (-> sankey); a hierarchy tree (that's navigation/side-menu-tree)

widget-grid.useWhen: a whole DASHBOARD: a draggable/resizable grid of widget tiles (vue-grid-layout)
widget-grid.dontUse: a single chart on a page (just place the chart); a static form layout (-> the 12-col grid)
widget-grid.example: an infra overview dashboard of charts + KPI tiles

do: Pick the type by the question the viewer is answering (decisionFlow), not by looks.
Colour multi-series charts from tokens/chart-palette.json IN ORDER; use severity tokens for status/threshold.
Render with the product's component: Chart (src/components/chart/chart.vue), Graph (monitor-graph/graph.vue), or Widgets (components/widgets). Reuse, don't re-engine.
Give every chart a loading, empty and error state; use data-viz-tooltips for hover detail.
Theme with DS tokens (--common-widget-bg tile surface, --page-text-color, --border-color) so it flips light/dark.
dont: Don't build a framework-agnostic obs-chart / obs-graph — the engines are licensed/heavy and app-coupled.
Don't colour a chart with the brand navy --primary; series must stay distinguishable (use the categorical palette).
Don't improvise a chart in a standalone prototype — STOP and ASK (the DS has no chart component).
Don't hand-roll a topology canvas or a widget grid — reuse Graph / Widgets.

a11y.summary: Charts must not rely on colour alone — pair series with labels/legend and expose the data as a table alternative where possible. Keyboard: the widget grid and topology canvas provide their own focus/zoom controls.
issues: Colour-only encoding fails colour-blind users — always label series and provide a legend.
Canvas-rendered charts/graphs are not screen-reader legible — offer the underlying data as a grid (ChartWithGrid) for critical views.

knownIssues: App-coupled: charts (Highcharts v10), topology (Cytoscape.js), dashboard grid (vue-grid-layout) are rendered by product components, not by the DS — there is intentionally no obs-* for them.
Highcharts is a COMMERCIALLY LICENSED engine — do not vendor it into a standalone prototype; that's why standalone chart requests are a STOP-and-ASK.
The categorical chart palette (chart-palette.json) is separate from the brand/token palette — don't conflate.

changelog.change: Closed the two chart-library gaps: (1) shipped configs are now DIRECTLY RENDERABLE — formatter/event «fn» markers stripped so Highcharts.chart(config) just works, with each fixture's stripped formatter slots recorded in $formatters + a real formatter library at charts/formatters.js (bytes/percent/bps/duration/dateTime + attachFormatters) for product-accurate labels; (2) confirmed the configs are THEME-ADAPTIVE via DS tokens (var(--…)) — same config in light+dark, no separate capture needed (added the missing --chart-font-family dark value).

Added the captured CHART LIBRARY (chartLibrary): 32 sanitised configs across 9 categories (time-series, top-n, distribution, anomaly, forecast, gauge, heat-map, map, sankey), now shipped in the spec package under charts/ + indexed in charts/manifest.json and live on the showcase. Turns the standalone "STOP and ASK" dead-end into copy-ready Highcharts v10 configs. Known gaps flagged (unserialised formatter fns; dark-theme capture).

changelog: 2026-07-23 — obs-metric-picker joined this family (owner): the charts/topology/grid stay decision GUIDES (no obs-*), but the metric SELECTOR that feeds them is a real shippable element and now lives here — the buildable authoring side of the data-viz workflow.

changelog.change: Examples charts now render through the product's real config pipeline (default-config + getWidgetChartCommonOptions) so they match the product (gridlines/legend/tooltip/palette) and theme with light/dark. Added the 6 non-Highcharts types via their real engines + static refs; hardened the gate with a theme-awareness probe.

Catalogued the data-viz family as a decision GUIDE (charts/stat-tiles/topology/widget-grid) — engine-backed, no obs-* by design. Added chart-palette tokens + type-selection decisionFlow + per-type usageRules.

usage.$note: 38 files mount <Chart> (Highcharts); 11 import chart.vue directly. Chart TYPES are config-driven (one Chart, many Highcharts `type`s), not distinct Vue components — counts are by render FAMILY, approximate.

chartLibrary.$note: The DS ships 32 CAPTURED chart configs across 9 categories (product chart-builder output, sanitised), under charts/ in this package (config JSON per fixture) with an index at charts/manifest.json, and live at the showcase …/elements/charts.html. HOW TO USE: pick the category below, take the fixture's config and render with Highcharts v10 (Highcharts.chart(el, config)); the custom-engine types (gauge, heat-map, anomaly, forecast, some map/top-n) carry a result payload drawn by a small custom renderer. The configs are DIRECTLY RENDERABLE: formatter/event FUNCTIONS were stripped (they cannot survive JSON) so labels use engine defaults — for product-accurate unit labels (bytes→GB, bits→Mbps, seconds→'2d 3h') attach a formatter from charts/formatters.js to the slots each fixture lists in $formatters (see attachFormatters). THEME: every colour is a DS token (var(--…)), so the SAME config renders in LIGHT and DARK when the DS theme CSS (@mtdt/observeops-ds-css) is loaded — no separate light/dark config. Colour series from the categorical palette / severity tokens, never the brand navy --primary.
chartLibrary.engine: Highcharts v10 (+ highcharts-more, solid-gauge, sankey, heatmap, treemap, map, no-data-to-display); Leaflet for the online map

categories.title: Time Series
categories.useWhen: trend over time — line/area/vertical+horizontal bar, each stacked; single- and multi-counter

categories.title: Top N Views
categories.useWhen: the leaders — solid-gauge grid, packed bubble, tree view (one payload drives all three)

categories.title: Distribution (Pie / Donut)
categories.useWhen: part-to-whole share — pie or donut (≤5 slices)

categories.title: Anomaly
categories.useWhen: AI/ML time series — actuals + confidence band, outliers coloured by zone

categories.title: Forecast
categories.useWhen: AI/ML projection past the last actual with a widening confidence range

categories.title: Gauge
categories.useWhen: single value vs a threshold/range — solid-gauge dial or numeric metro tile

categories.title: Heat Map
categories.useWhen: density across two dimensions (host × metric) — severity honeycomb

categories.title: Map
categories.useWhen: geography — country-intensity bubbles / labelled points, or the online Leaflet map

categories.title: Sankey
categories.useWhen: flow/volume between source and destination nodes
